title: Maser emission from the CO envelope of the asymptotic giant branch star W Hydrae
question: Is there CO maser emission in the J=3-2 line around the AGB star W Hya, where does it come from, and what pumps it

data.angular_resolution: 31x21 mas (-63 deg from north) and 29x21 mas (-68 deg) for the two epochs
data.sensitivity: rms ~3.5 mJy/beam near the CO line in both epochs

what.value: CO envelope model parameters of the baseline model (Table 1) and distance adopted from the model

evidence.quote: taken from (cite: Khouri14); we do not adjust the distance and adopt the value used in the model.

what.value: CO transition frequencies, energy levels, Einstein coefficients and collisional rate coefficients

evidence.quote: The transition frequencies, energy levels, and Einstein coefficients were taken from the CDMS and JPL databases (cite: Muller01; Picket98) and the collisional rate coefficients come from (cite: Yang10).

what.value: Observed 4.6 micron infrared spectrum used to constrain pump radiation (85% transmission of the stellar black body)

evidence.quote: Based on observations around 4.6 $\mu$m (cite: Justtanont14) we include an overall decrease in the stellar radiation field around this wavelength, adopting a transmission of 85% of the stellar black body.

recipe.goal: calibrate and self-calibrate the ALMA band 7 data
recipe.method: manual calibration scripts from the observatory, then two rounds of phase self-calibration on the stellar continuum
key_parameters: continuum S/N improved by a factor of three

recipe.goal: image the CO J=3-2 line at matched resolution in both epochs
recipe.method: Briggs weighting with robust -1.0 (epoch 1) and 0.5 (epoch 2) to obtain similar angular resolution
key_parameters: beams 31x21 mas and 29x21 mas; rms ~3.5 mJy/beam

recipe.goal: measure maser brightness temperature, optical depth, line width, morphology and variability
recipe.method: subtract the stellar continuum, measure peak Tb in the emission maps, extract single-beam spectra at the peak, and image the three days of epoch 1 separately with a common beam
key_parameters: stellar continuum brightness temperature ~2700 K subtracted
assumptions: maser amplifies the underlying stellar continuum, so Tb implies optical depth tau
if the emission is compact or made of multiple components, Tb is a lower limit

recipe.goal: compare maser velocity with other masers of W Hya
recipe.method: compare the CO maser velocity with literature OH and H2O maser peak velocities
assumptions: a common velocity reflects the largest coherent velocity path length towards the star, giving an amplified stellar image in many maser species

recipe.goal: model continuum pumping with 1-D radiative transfer
recipe.method: one-dimensional Monte Carlo radiative transfer of CO with the baseline envelope model of Khouri14, observed through a single aperture of size 2R* towards the star, with the extended-atmosphere CO absorption profile added on top of the stellar black body; then multiply the radiation field below 5 micron by a factor M
key_parameters: M~3 gives a maser of sufficient strength; need V0~4.2 km/s, beta~2.5, Vt~1.0 km/s to match maser velocity and width
assumptions: model is one-dimensional so only emission along the line of sight to the star is compared; distance not adjusted from the adopted model value

recipe.goal: constrain mass-loss rate range and test dust-shell pumping
recipe.method: vary the mass-loss rate in the maser model and compare with the lower resolution (ACA) observations; add a dust shell to supply the 4.6 micron excess and check against the observed infrared spectrum

recipe.goal: test line-overlap pumping of the v=0-1 4.6 micron lines
recipe.method: change the relative radiation field seen by individual v=0-1 IR lines (J=0 to 5) in the model, with an 85% transmission of the stellar black body near 4.6 micron
assumptions: the observed single transition can be reproduced by many different combinations of relative IR pumping

answer_key.quantity: maser peak brightness temperature (after continuum subtraction)

evidence.quote: the peak of the emission has a brightness temperature of $T_b\approx1950$ K in the two epochs.
the brightness temperatures imply a maser optical depth of $\tau\approx-0.55$.

answer_key.quantity: FWHM of the brightest spectral component (epoch 1, epoch 2)

evidence.quote: The brightest spectral component has a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of $1.9$ and $2.2$ km s$^{-1}$ in the two epochs, respectively.
The velocity of the CO maser remained stable at $\sim35$ km s$^{-1}$ over the two epochs with a FWHM velocity width of $\sim2$ km s$^{-1}$.

answer_key.quantity: brightness temperature on 30 Nov, 3 Dec, 5 Dec 2015

evidence.quote: The emission brightness temperature appears to change from $T_b\approx1330$ K on 30 Nov to $T_b\approx2000$ K on 3 Dec and to $T_b\approx1570$ K on 5 Dec 2015.
This indicates that there could be variability of the order of $\pm20\%$ within only a five-day timescale.

answer_key.quantity: continuum flux variation over the three days

evidence.quote: the continuum flux varies by less than $2.5\%$ over the three days

answer_key.quantity: radiation field boost factor at 4.6 micron needed for a maser of sufficient strength

evidence.quote: a maser of sufficient strength can be generated if the radiation field at 4.6 $\mu$m is increased by a factor $M\sim3$.
we require a larger velocity at the inner envelope ($V_0\approx4.2$ km s$^{-1}$)
larger turbulent velocity component ($V_t\approx 1.0$ km s$^{-1}$)

answer_key.quantity: radius where J=3-2 population inversion peaks

evidence.quote: Population inversion in the $J=3-2$ line persists throughout most of the CSE and peaks around $7$ au.

answer_key.quantity: mass-loss rate range generating maser emission in the model

evidence.quote: maser emission is generated, from different parts of the envelope, for mass-loss rates between $0.5-5\times10^{-7}$ M$_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$.

answer_key.quantity: mass-loss rate of W Hya allowed by lower resolution data

evidence.quote: limiting the rate to between $1.5-3.0\times10^{-7}$ M$_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$.

answer_key.quantity: dust-shell optical depth at 4.6 micron needed to reproduce the continuum excess

evidence.quote: a dust shell with an optical depth at 4.6 $\mu$m of $\sim0.2$

score_reason: Project codes, dates, on-source times, robust values and beams are given, and the main results are numeric, but calibrators, self-cal solints, continuum subtraction and imaging parameters are deferred to earlier papers or omitted, and the radiative transfer models are hand-tuned with partial inputs
